newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky-trade pact will expand global telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky-trade pact will expand global telecoms.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative designate Charlene Barshefsky on Saturday said a landmark agreement opening telecommunication markets around the world could double or triple the size of the $600 billion telecommunications industry over the next decade.
"U.S. companies are the most competitive telecommunications providers in the world; they are in the best position to compete and win under this agreement," Barshefsky told a news conference.

"We expect the agreement will lead to the creation of approximately a million U.S. jobs in the next 10 years -- not only in communications companies but also in high-tech equipment makers and in a range of industries such as software, information services and electronic publishing that benefit from telecom development," Barshefsky said.

She spoke in Washington shortly after negotiators in Geneva representing some 70 countries reached a breakthrough global telecommunications trade agreement after months of talks under the auspices of the World Trade Organisation.

The accord, which covers more than 95 percent of world telecommunications revenue, ensures that U.S. companies can compete against and invest in all of the world's existing telecommunications carriers, Barshefsky said.
Before the agreement was reached, only 17 percent of the top telecom markets were open to U.S. companies, she said. Now they have access to nearly 100 percent of those markets, she added.
